correctness.rationale: For any vertex subset S, if the unique center belongs to S, S is secure exactly when at most one peripheral matching edge avoids S; without the center, every peripheral pair must be represented. Necessity follows from forcing a swap of the center to defend a vertex in an untouched pair; sufficiency is furnished by specified defending swaps. The quotient edge for each peripheral pair encodes these counts for unions of partition classes, including loops. In the upper-bound proof there are two distinct quotient edges avoiding the center class. If disjoint, any non-center class outside their four endpoint supports has no partner. If intersecting, their union U and intersection I bound exterior classes by |I| via an injective partner assignment, with |U|+|I|<=4. The explicit center-plus-(m-2)-pairs construction and four peripheral singletons achieves five classes. Exhaustive direct guard exchanges match the secure-set criterion for 2<=m<=7 and all set partitions for 2<=m<=5. The unrestricted result follows from the proof, not finite experiments. The public definition permits a secure singleton exception only when the singleton is itself securely dominating; the universal hub singleton is not securely dominating for m>=2 and, like all other blocks, must have a valid nonsecure partner. This strict condition is imposed in the quotient criterion and independent enumeration.

originality.rationale: The first public 2025 secure-coalition manuscript introduces SEC, proves a generic lower bound of delta(G)+2 and upper bound n-gamma_s(G)+2, and classifies certain extremal cases and trees. On friendship graphs these imply at most 4<=SEC(F_m)<=m+3, not the constant-five formula for m>=3. Its available full-text search and inspected sections did not give a friendship-graph formula or this quotient classification. Standard ordinary coalitions are mathematically weaker than secure coalitions. Targeted graph-alias and invariant searches plus mathematical finding records did not identify an equivalent stronger theorem, but absence of hits is not priority certification.

value.rationale: The freshly introduced secure coalition number is determined exactly throughout a natural unbounded connected graph family, replacing a size-dependent bound m+3 by a constant sharp value 5 for all m>=2. A nontrivial quotient-incidence theorem distinguishes disjoint from intersecting forbidden pair supports and recognizes all secure-coalition partitions, not merely the extremal parameter. The result is a structural graph-family theorem rather than a small finite example or an arbitrary specialization; its two-edge obstruction supplies a method potentially reusable for graphs formed by joined sparse components.
